title: Pre-orders for a small bakery
brief: I run a bakery with two staff. Customers keep phoning in orders for weekend cakes and we lose track. I'd like a simple page where people can pick what they want for Saturday or Sunday, say when they'll collect it, and leave a name and phone number. Each evening I want to see what we need to bake tomorrow.

implicitRequirements.text: Orders for a day close at a cut-off the day before (the baker needs time to bake), and the page says so.
An item that has sold out for that day cannot be ordered any more.
The customer is told clearly that the order went through, with what they ordered and the collection time.
The baker's daily list adds up quantities per item, not just a list of orders.
A phone number that is obviously wrong is caught before the order is taken.
Nobody pays online; the page must not ask for card details.

title: A volunteer rota for a food bank
brief: Our food bank has about forty volunteers. Right now the rota is a spreadsheet that three people edit and it's always wrong. Volunteers should be able to see open shifts and sign up, and the coordinator should see who is on each shift.

implicitRequirements.text: A shift has a maximum number of volunteers and cannot be over-filled.
A volunteer cannot be booked on two shifts at the same time.
Volunteers can cancel, and the freed place becomes available again.
The coordinator is warned about shifts that are short of people close to the day.
Volunteers only see first names of others, not phone numbers.

title: A reading log for a primary class
brief: I teach a class of 28 eight-year-olds. I want them to log the books they read at home, how many pages, and a star rating, and I want to see who is reading and who isn't. Parents sometimes fill it in for younger ones.

implicitRequirements.text: Children's full names and details are not visible to other children.
Page counts that are impossible (negative, or thousands in a day) are refused or flagged.
The teacher's view highlights children who have logged nothing for a while.
Entering a log is simple enough for an eight-year-old: few fields, forgiving input.
Data from last school year can be archived without deleting it.

title: A donor list and thank-you letters for a charity
brief: We're a small charity. When someone donates we want to record it and send a thank-you letter. At the end of the year we'd like a total per donor for their records.

implicitRequirements.text: A donor who asked not to be contacted never gets a letter.
Amounts are stored exactly (no rounding errors) and totals per year add up to the donations.
The same person giving twice is recognised as one donor, not two.
Letters can be printed or emailed, and it is recorded which was sent.
Personal data can be exported or removed for a donor who asks.

title: Expense approvals for a team
brief: Our team of twelve submits expenses by email to the manager. Build an internal tool where people submit an expense with a receipt, a manager approves or rejects with a reason, and finance can export approved expenses monthly.

implicitRequirements.text: Someone cannot approve their own expense.
A rejected expense can be corrected and resubmitted, keeping its history.
Amounts carry a currency, and the monthly export does not mix currencies silently.
Every approval and rejection is recorded with who did it and when.
An expense already exported cannot be edited afterwards.

title: An internal status page
brief: We run about ten internal services. We want a page that shows whether each is up, with a short history, so people stop asking in chat.

implicitRequirements.text: A service that has not reported for a while is shown as unknown, not as up.
A single failed check does not flip a service to down; a few in a row do.
Times are shown in the viewer's time zone, not the server's.
The page itself keeps working when one of the services it checks is slow.
History is kept for a bounded period and does not grow forever.

title: A command-line tool to rename photos by date
brief: I have thousands of photos named IMG_1234.JPG. Write a small command-line tool that renames them to the date they were taken, like 2024-06-01_14-03-22.jpg.

implicitRequirements.text: Two photos taken in the same second do not overwrite each other.
Nothing is renamed without a way to preview what would happen first.
Photos without a date in their metadata are left alone and reported.
Running it twice does not rename already-renamed photos again.
It never deletes a file.

title: Feature flags for our web app
brief: We want to turn features on and off in production without deploying, and roll a feature out to a percentage of users.

implicitRequirements.text: The same user keeps seeing the same side of a percentage rollout across visits.
If the flag service is unreachable, the app falls back to a safe default instead of failing.
Changing a flag is recorded with who changed it.
A flag can be turned off instantly for everyone as a kill switch.
Unknown flag names are reported rather than silently treated as on.

title: Forward webhooks to our team chat
brief: When our payment provider sends us a webhook about a failed payment, post a short message in our team chat channel.

implicitRequirements.text: Webhooks with a bad signature are ignored, not posted.
The same webhook delivered twice produces one message.
Customer card numbers or full emails never appear in the chat message.
If the chat service is down, messages are retried later rather than lost.
Only the event types we care about are posted.

title: A notes app that works offline
brief: A simple markdown notes app for myself: write notes, tag them, search them. It should work on the train without internet.

implicitRequirements.text: Notes written offline are not lost when the app closes.
Search finds words inside notes, not just titles, and is fast with thousands of notes.
Editing the same note on two devices does not silently drop one version.
Deleted notes can be recovered for a while.
Notes can be exported as plain markdown files.

title: Appointment reminders for a physiotherapy clinic
brief: We're a clinic with three physios. Patients forget appointments. We'd like reminders sent the day before by text message, and patients able to reply to cancel.

implicitRequirements.text: Reminders are sent at a sensible local time, not in the middle of the night.
A patient who has opted out never receives a reminder.
A cancellation by reply frees the slot and tells the clinic.
Reminder texts do not include medical details.
An appointment moved after the reminder was sent gets a corrected reminder.

title: Invoices for a freelance illustrator
brief: I'm a freelance illustrator. I want to make invoices for clients from a template, number them, and see which ones are still unpaid.

implicitRequirements.text: Invoice numbers are sequential and never reused, even if an invoice is cancelled.
Totals, tax and discounts add up exactly on the invoice.
Once sent, an invoice is not edited; a correction is a credit note or a new invoice.
Unpaid invoices past their due date are clearly marked.
The illustrator's bank details appear on the invoice exactly as entered.
